title: Comparison: two Kotlin 2.4 articles, then a navigation choice
description: The user compares what two Medium articles say about upgrading to Kotlin 2.4 ('the comparison' and 'the feature list'), corrects a detail about the team, then changes direction to choosing a navigation approach for a Compose Multiplatform app (1.7.0 type-safe navigation vs 1.10.0 Navigation 3) — after which the memory must let go of the Kotlin 2.4 focus.

messages.user: I need to decide whether our team should upgrade to Kotlin 2.4 now. Two articles cover it: 'Kotlin 2.4 vs Kotlin 2.3: What Actually Changed?' and 'Kotlin 2.4: 10 New Features Android Developers Should Know'. What does each one call the most important change?

knowledge_database/Kotlin 2.4_ 10 New Features Android Developers Should Know _ Medium.html
facts: Both articles put stable context parameters first

messages.user: What does the comparison say about whether we should upgrade right now?

sources: knowledge_database/Kotlin 2.4 vs Kotlin 2.3_ What Actually Changed_ _ Medium.html
facts: Kotlin 2.4 requires Gradle 9.5.0 or newer, so check Gradle compatibility and update Android Studio
Adopt context parameters incrementally rather than rewriting everything at once

(First version asked what to 'check before upgrading'; the feature list has no such checks, so the follow-up 'And the other one?' was honestly declined — reworded to the upgrade advice both articles give.)

facts: Context parameters and explicit backing fields are a safe, backward-compatible win for MVVM or Clean Architecture codebases
The major structural advantages go to multiplatform teams; single-platform Android apps get mainly ergonomic and modest performance gains
